original_test_intent: Verify the distinct 16-bit SMBIOS Type 4 Core Count 2 field is present when the structure version/length supports it, carries the approved physical-core count and is used consistently with the legacy Core Count selector before and after reboot.
original_method: Capture raw Type 4 bytes plus decoded output, verify formatted length reaches Core Count 2, extract the extended UINT16 by structure definition rather than text label, validate its relationship to the legacy Core Count byte and approved topology, reboot and repeat.
manual_activity: A user approves the expected extended values, applicable SMBIOS structure revision, legacy-selector rule and reboot plan. Raw field extraction and validation are automatable.
required_inputs: Applicable SMBIOS version and minimum Type 4 formatted length for Core Count 2
Expected 16-bit Core Count 2 per populated socket
Exact relationship required between legacy Core Count and Core Count 2, including extended-value selector use
Approved physical-core topology and any unknown/not-supported policy
Validated raw SMBIOS parser plus approved reboot and OOB recovery plan
safety_requirements: Read SMBIOS only; do not change core controls, CPU state, SMT or firmware.
Do not rely on the literal `CoreCount2` grep token or assume a decoder displays the extended field separately; preserve raw structure bytes and offsets.
Reject reading beyond formatted length and retain both legacy byte and extended UINT16 in evidence.
Validate the extended field itself even if dmidecode presents only a normalized `Core Count` line; normalized output is not proof of field encoding.
Stop on unsupported length, invalid selector relationship, socket mismatch, drift or reboot failure; no automatic retry.
agent_execution_scope: Extract Core Count 2 from raw Type 4 structures by version/length-aware definition, validate legacy-selector consistency and compare approved values before/after reboot.
Do not substitute the normalized Core Count display, alter topology or decide PASS/FAIL.
engineer_actions: Approve the applicable extended-field specification, expected per-socket values and legacy-selector semantics.
Approve reboot/recovery and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The literal `CoreCount2` label is not reliable and may produce empty evidence or miss a decoder-normalized extended value; it does not inspect raw structure length or offset.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Use a validated raw SMBIOS Type 4 parser to retain formatted length, legacy Core Count byte and the Core Count 2 UINT16; keep dmidecode output as secondary decoded evidence.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The distinct CoreCount2 field scope, Type 4 script and 10/10-minute values are retained.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Parse Core Count 2 directly from each sufficiently long Type 4 formatted section, validate little-endian raw bytes and legacy-selector consistency, then compare the 16-bit value per socket before and after reboot.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: SMBIOS Type 4 implementations whose revision and formatted length include Core Count 2.
modernized_recommendation.supported_version: Record SMBIOS, Type 4 length, BIOS, CPU topology and raw-parser/dmidecode versions.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Applicable SMBIOS Type 4 Core Count 2 field layout and legacy Core Count selection semantics, approved CPU topology and installed parser documentation.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Replaces an unreliable literal text-label filter with direct field-level raw validation while retaining the original extended-field purpose.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: Improves coverage by proving the encoded extended field and selector relationship rather than only a normalized display value.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Version/length/offset rule and expected extended values.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Some decoders intentionally hide the separate extended field; raw parsing is required and must be version/length guarded.

project_override_considerations: A project may declare the extended field not applicable only when the approved SMBIOS revision/Type 4 length excludes it; on a supporting structure, the test must validate the actual field rather than fall back silently to legacy Core Count.
expected_evidence: Approved SMBIOS/Type 4 field definition, per-socket Core Count 2 baseline, selector rule and parser versions
Complete pre-reboot raw Type 4 bytes with handle/socket, formatted length, legacy byte, extended UINT16 and decoded effective count
Field-presence, offset and legacy/extended consistency results
Approved reboot/health evidence and equivalent post-reboot raw comparison
Engineer verdict or explicit approved not-applicable determination based on structure revision/length

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: `CoreCount2` is a compact spelling of the standardized extended field and is semantically resolvable; the DeepSeek text filter is inadequate but does not create an irreducible source conflict.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The field can be reviewed and extracted safely with a version/length-aware raw parser; missing baseline/parser is readiness input.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Rejects the unreliable literal-label grep and requires raw field/length evidence.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its extended-field interpretation but strengthens it to direct encoding validation and corrects capability to FULLY AUTOMATABLE.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Ensures this dedicated field case is not collapsed into the preceding effective Core Count case.

review_improvement: Preserves the independent coverage of Core Count 2 and detects malformed selector/extended encodings that normalized decoder output could conceal.
independent_technical_reasoning: Once field definition and expected values are approved, raw extraction, bounds checking, selector validation and reboot comparison are deterministic software tasks.
